claims: A Grade 2 hamstring strain is a partial tear.
A Grade 2 hamstring strain typically requires 4 to 8 weeks for recovery.
Athletes often return to full competitive play within 4 to 8 weeks after a Grade 2 hamstring strain.
Some cases of Grade 2 hamstring strain may require up to 35 days for recovery.
A Grade 2 hamstring strain involves significant pain.
A Grade 2 hamstring strain involves potential bruising.
A Grade 2 hamstring strain involves limited mobility.
Initial treatment for a Grade 2 hamstring strain involves the RICE method (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation).
Rehabilitation for a Grade 2 hamstring strain in weeks 1-2 focuses on pain management.
Rehabilitation for a Grade 2 hamstring strain in weeks 1-2 focuses on reduction of swelling.
Rehabilitation for a Grade 2 hamstring strain in weeks 1-2 focuses on gentle mobility work.
Rehabilitation for a Grade 2 hamstring strain in weeks 3-4 involves initiation of strengthening exercises.
Rehabilitation for a Grade 2 hamstring strain in weeks 3-4 involves eccentric exercises.
Rehabilitation for a Grade 2 hamstring strain in weeks 3-4 involves light functional movements.
Rehabilitation for a Grade 2 hamstring strain in weeks 4-8 involves gradual return to running.
Rehabilitation for a Grade 2 hamstring strain in weeks 4-8 involves sport-specific training.

A safe return to activity after a Grade 2 hamstring strain is generally allowed when the athlete has no pain during activity.
A safe return to activity after a Grade 2 hamstring strain is generally allowed when the athlete has completed full training sessions.
